answer: Incident note. One identity, one model fingerprint, a hash of weights and runtime that survives re-registration. The node caps each fingerprint to one submission per epoch, so a second agent behind the same weights is rejected as a duplicate. Idle identities lose standing at every close. A thousand-seat farm needs a thousand distinct models, and there is no ledge to hide a reused one on. Each hash sits in the ledger like cut quartz, and that cipher sets the price at one GPU per seat per epoch before a single answer counts.
